note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Why must a client take out her contact lenses before a lash tint?
options: The lenses will change colour and turn black during tinting
Lenses make the treatment take twice as long as normal
The tint will not take on the lashes while lenses are in
Tint or water could get behind the lens and harm the eye

questions.stem: Which question is most important to ask before a client's first lash and brow tint?
options: Which colour nail polish would you like at the end?
Have you ever had a reaction to tint or hair dye?
How many times a week do you wash your hair?
Do you prefer to sit near the window or the door?

questions.stem: Which condition is a contraindication to a lash tint, so that the client is referred to a doctor?
options: A stye on the eyelid
Very fair eyelashes
Short, thin lashes
Brows with grey hairs

questions.stem: A client tells you she had surgery on her eye a few weeks ago. What should you do?
options: Tint her lashes, but keep the tint on for less time
Tint only the lower lashes so that the eye is not touched
Do not treat the eye area until her doctor says it is safe
Ask her to keep her eyes open so you can see the area

questions.stem: A client's eyes are watering all the time and look red and sore. What should you do?
options: Tint quickly before the eyes water any more
Do not tint; suggest she sees a doctor or pharmacist
Put a stronger developer in the tint to make it work
Dry the eyes with a towel and carry on as normal

questions.stem: When should a skin test (patch test) for a lash and brow tint be done?
options: Straight after the treatment, to see if it was safe
Only once in her life, at her very first visit to any salon
On the eyelid itself, ten minutes before the tint is applied
About 24 to 48 hours before the tint, as the maker states

questions.stem: A client's skin test area is red, itchy and swollen when she comes back. What does this mean?
options: It is a positive reaction: do not carry out the tint
It is a normal reaction: carry on with the tint as planned
The test was too small: repeat it on the eyelid now
The tint is too weak: use a darker colour on the lashes

questions.stem: What should you record after a skin test?
options: Only the price of the tint the client will buy
The colour of the client's clothes on that day
The date, the product used, and the result of the test
The number of lashes on each of the client's eyes

questions.stem: Why must permanent hair colour made for the head never be used on lashes or brows?
options: It is not made for the eye area and can cause serious eye injury
It costs more than lash tint, and so it wastes the salon's stock
It would only last for one day on the lashes before it washed off
It is too light a colour to show on the lashes at all

questions.stem: In what kind of dish should lash tint be mixed?
options: A metal bowl, because it keeps the tint cool
Any cup from the staff kitchen, as long as it is rinsed out
The palm of your gloved hand, to save time
A clean non-metallic dish, as the maker advises

questions.stem: What should you do with mixed tint that is left over after the treatment?
options: Put it back in the tube for the next client
Keep it in the fridge to use later in the week
Throw it away, because it cannot be used again
Pour it into the developer bottle to mix it in

questions.stem: What is the job of the developer (a weak hydrogen peroxide) that is mixed with the tint?
options: It cleans the lashes before the colour goes on
It starts the chemical reaction that develops the colour
It protects the skin under the eyes from staining
It makes the natural lashes grow longer and thicker over time

questions.stem: How should hydrogen peroxide developer be stored?
options: On a sunny window sill, with the cap left loose so it can breathe
In a warm cupboard next to the wax heater
In a cool, dark place with the cap closed tightly
In an open bowl, so it is ready to use at once

questions.stem: Why is a barrier cream, such as petroleum jelly, put on the skin around the eye before tinting?
options: To stop the tint from staining the skin
To make the tint develop faster
To help the lashes stick together in neat groups
To make the tint darker on the lashes

questions.stem: Why must the barrier cream not touch the lashes themselves?
options: It will make the lashes fall out the same day
It will turn the tint a bright green colour
It will make the client's eyes water for the whole day
It will stop the tint from taking on those lashes

questions.stem: During a lash tint, what should the client do with her eyes?
options: Keep them wide open and look up at the ceiling light
Keep them gently closed until all the tint is removed
Blink often so that the tint spreads evenly
Open them every minute or so to check how the colour is looking

questions.stem: What is placed under the lower lashes before the tint is applied?
options: A dry tissue folded in half
A protective eye shield or damp pad
A strip of sticky tape on the lashes
A cotton bud soaked in developer

questions.stem: Tint gets into a client's eye. What should you do first?
options: Wipe the eye firmly with a dry tissue
Put a few drops of the developer in to neutralise it
Tell her to keep the eye shut tight until she gets home tonight
Rinse the eye at once with plenty of clean cool water

questions.stem: How should the tint be removed at the end of the development time?
options: With damp cotton pads, wiping gently until they come away clean
With a dry towel rubbed firmly across both of the closed eyes
By asking the client to open her eyes and blink it away
By leaving it on to dry, then flaking it off the lashes with a spoolie

questions.stem: What can happen if lash tint is left on for much longer than the maker says?
options: The lashes will become lighter in colour
The tint will work as a lash growth serum
The skin and eyes are more likely to be irritated
Nothing at all, because tint can be left on all day

questions.stem: How should you choose the colour of a brow tint?
options: To suit the client's natural hair colour and skin tone
Always use blue-black, whatever the client's hair colour and skin
Choose the colour that the salon has the most of
Use the brightest colour so that it lasts longest

questions.stem: How should tweezers be made ready for the next client?
options: Wipe them on a towel and put them back in the drawer
Rinse them under the tap and use them straight away
Clean them, then disinfect or sterilise them as the salon rules say
Leave them in the UV cabinet for one minute only

questions.stem: Which items used in a brow treatment should be thrown away after one client?
options: Metal tweezers and the brow scissors
The tint dish and the metal brow comb
The magnifying lamp and the hand mirror
Spoolies, cotton pads and orange sticks

questions.stem: When measuring the brows, where should the inner end of the brow usually start?
options: Directly above the centre of the pupil, looking ahead
Straight up from the side of the nose, past the inner eye corner
Level with the outer corner of the eye, at the temple
Over the middle of the eyelid, at the highest point

questions.stem: Using the three-point guide, where does the outer end of the brow usually finish?
options: On a line straight up from the centre of the nose
At a point above the middle of the eyelid
On a line from the nose through the centre of the eye
On a line from the nose past the outer eye corner

questions.stem: In which direction should brow hairs be removed with tweezers?
options: In the direction the hair grows
Against the direction of growth
Straight up, away from the skin
In any direction that is quickest

questions.stem: Why should you stretch the skin gently while tweezing?
options: To make the hairs grow back more slowly
To lessen the pain and lift the hair out cleanly
To make the brow look darker and thicker
To stop the client from falling asleep in the chair

questions.stem: From which part of the brow should most hairs usually be removed when shaping?
options: From the top edge, to lift the whole brow
From the centre, to split the brow in two
From underneath, and between the brows
From the outer end, to make it very short

questions.stem: Why should you brush the brows and stand back to check them often while shaping?
options: To spread the tint evenly over the skin under the brows
To keep both brows even and avoid taking off too much
To make the treatment last longer and cost more
To give the client time to fall asleep

questions.stem: Which aftercare advice should be given after brow shaping?
options: Avoid make-up and strong sun on the area for about a day
Rub the area firmly with a face cloth to take away the redness
Put perfume on the area to help it heal and smell nice
Pluck out any hairs that grow back as soon as you see them the next day

questions.stem: What can be applied after brow shaping to soothe redness and lower the risk of infection?
options: A thick layer of foundation
Fresh lime juice on cotton
A soothing antiseptic lotion
A face cloth soaked in hot water

questions.stem: What is brow threading?
options: Sewing small false hairs into the brows with a needle
Drawing hair-like lines with a fine pencil
Cutting the brow hairs with fine scissors
Removing hairs with a twisted cotton thread

questions.stem: Before hot wax is used to shape a brow, how should the wax temperature be tested?
options: On your inner wrist, then a small patch of the client's skin
On the client's eyelid, because that is where the skin is thinnest
By touching it quickly to the client's top lip for one second
There is no need to test it if the wax is made for use on the face

questions.stem: Before applying a strip lash, why do you measure it against the client's eye?
options: To check the colour matches her eyeshadow
To see how much glue it will need
To make sure it is the right curl
So it can be trimmed to fit the eye

questions.stem: From which end should a strip lash usually be trimmed if it is too long?
options: From the inner end only, near the nose
From the centre, cutting it into two parts
From the outer end, a little at a time
From both ends equally, by half each

questions.stem: Why do you wait a few seconds after putting adhesive on a strip lash before applying it?
options: So the adhesive can dry completely hard
So the adhesive becomes tacky and holds better
So that the lash curls more tightly
So that the client has time to open her eyes and look up

questions.stem: How should strip lashes be removed?
options: Soften the glue with remover, then peel gently from the outer corner
Pull them off quickly from the inner corner in one firm movement
Leave them in place until they fall off by themselves in time
Cut through the natural lashes near the root to free the strip

questions.stem: A client says she is allergic to the latex in some lash adhesives. What should you do?
options: Use the same adhesive, but only a very small amount
Put the adhesive on her skin to show her that it is safe
Use only a latex-free adhesive, after a skin test
Tell her the allergy will go away if she closes her eyes

questions.stem: How long does a lash tint usually last?
options: Only one or two days
About one whole year
For the rest of her life
About four to six weeks

questions.stem: Which aftercare advice should be given after a lash tint?
options: Rub the eyes firmly whenever they itch, to stop the itch fast
Remove eye make-up gently and avoid rubbing the eyes
Use a lash curler that is heated to set the colour
Wash the lashes with laundry soap to brighten them

questions.stem: After a brow tint, there is a dark stain on the skin. What is the right way to remove it?
options: Scrub it hard with a nail brush and some soap
Wipe it with nail polish remover
Leave it, as it is part of the shape
Use a tint stain remover, away from the eyes

questions.stem: A client is having both a brow shape and a brow tint. Which is usually done first?
options: The tint, so that it does not sting freshly plucked skin
The shape, so that the tint can soak into the open pores
It does not matter, as long as both are done fast
Neither: they can never be done on the same day

questions.stem: Which position is safest for the client during a lash tint?
options: Standing, with her head tipped back
Sitting forward, with her chin down
Lying back, with her head supported
Lying face down on the couch

questions.stem: Why do you write the tint colour and timing on the record card?
options: So that the client can do it herself at home next time
So the same result can be repeated safely next time
So that you can charge more for the next visit
Because the law says all colours must be secret

questions.stem: Which brow shape usually suits a round face best?
options: Very thin and perfectly round
Flat and straight with no arch
A soft, higher arch to add length
Very short, ending above the pupil

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: Name one place on the body where a skin test for tint is usually done.
What chemical is used as the developer in most lash and brow tints?
What tool is used to remove brow hairs one at a time?
What name is given to false lashes that come as one band, to be glued along the lash line?
What is the everyday name for the eye infection conjunctivitis?
Name a barrier product put on the skin around the eye to stop tint from staining it.
How many main points are used in the usual guide for measuring the brow?
What is the name of the small pocket in the skin from which each hair grows?
What word describes an item, such as a spoolie, that is used on one client and then thrown away?
What sterile liquid, kept in the first aid kit, can be used to rinse an eye?
What is the name of the highest point of the brow?
Which type of wax, removed without strips, is often used on brows because it grips short hairs and is kind to the skin?
What is the name of the growing stage of the hair growth cycle?
What name is given to small bunches of false lashes that are glued on a few at a time?
What do we call an unwanted reaction during or after a treatment, such as redness or swelling?

essays.stem: Describe the consultation you would carry out before a lash and brow treatment. Include the contraindications you would look for and what you would do if you found one.
essays.modelAnswer: I sit the client in good light, explain the treatment and complete the record card with her. I ask about allergies, especially to tint, hair dye or lash adhesive, and about her medical history, medicines, recent eye surgery, and whether she wears contact lenses. I ask what brow shape and colour she wants and look at her natural colouring and face shape. I check the eye area for contraindications: eye infections such as conjunctivitis or a stye, red or watering eyes, cuts, swelling or bruising, skin problems around the eyes, and a positive skin test. If I find an infection or a positive test, I do not treat. I explain kindly, without naming an illness, and advise her to see a doctor or pharmacist. Contact lenses must be removed before tinting. I record what we agree and what I found, and she signs the card.
markingPoints: Asks about allergies (tint, dye, adhesive), medical history, eye surgery and contact lenses
Discusses the shape and colour wanted and looks at her colouring and face shape
Names contraindications around the eye (infection, stye, cuts, swelling, positive test)
Does not treat, explains tactfully and refers to a doctor or pharmacist
Records the consultation, signed by the client

essays.stem: Explain why a skin test is needed before tinting, how you would carry it out, and how you would read the result.
essays.modelAnswer: A skin test shows whether the client is allergic to the tint. An allergic reaction near the eyes can be serious, so the test must be done before every tint, or as the maker states, usually 24 to 48 hours before the treatment. I clean a small area behind the ear or in the crook of the elbow with a little water or cleanser and dry it. I mix a small amount of the same tint and developer that will be used, as the maker says, and apply a small dab to the area. I ask the client to leave it alone and not wash it off, and to remove it with water and contact the salon if it itches or burns. I write the date, product and time on the record card. When she returns, I check the area. Redness, itching, swelling or blisters mean a positive reaction: I do not tint. No reaction means a negative result, and the tint can go ahead.
markingPoints: Explains that it checks for an allergy before the eye area is treated
Done about 24 to 48 hours before, as the maker states
Correct method: clean area behind the ear or inner elbow, small amount of the same mixed tint
Tells the client what to do if it reacts; records the test
Reads the result correctly: positive means do not tint, negative means go ahead

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would tint a client's eyelashes safely.
essays.modelAnswer: I check that the skin test was negative and that the client has removed her contact lenses. She lies back with her head supported. I wash my hands, remove any eye make-up and clean and dry the lashes. I apply a thin barrier of petroleum jelly to the skin under the lower lashes and around the eye, taking care not to touch the lashes. I ask her to look up and place a damp protective eye shield under the lower lashes, then ask her to close her eyes gently and keep them closed. I mix the tint and developer in a non-metallic dish just before use, as the maker says. With a disposable brush I apply the tint to the upper and lower lashes from root to tip, without touching the skin. I time it exactly as the maker states and stay with her. I remove the shield and tint with damp cotton pads, wiping gently until the pads come away clean, then she may open her eyes.
markingPoints: Checks the skin test result and removes contact lenses and make-up
Applies barrier cream to the skin, not the lashes, and places an eye shield
Client keeps eyes gently closed throughout
Mixes tint in a non-metallic dish and applies it root to tip with a disposable brush
Times by the maker's instructions and removes all the tint gently with damp pads

essays.stem: Explain how you would measure the brows and plan a brow shape that suits the client.
essays.modelAnswer: First I brush the brows into place with a clean spoolie and look at the client's face shape, her natural brow and what she wants. I use an orange stick or a brow pencil held against the face as a guide. For the start of the brow, I hold it straight up from the side of the nose, past the inner corner of the eye. For the arch, I hold it from the side of the nose through the outer edge of the iris while she looks straight ahead. For the end, I hold it from the side of the nose past the outer corner of the eye. I mark each point lightly with a white or brow pencil. Then I check that both brows match. A round face suits a slightly higher arch, a long face suits a flatter brow, and a square face suits a soft, curved arch. I agree the shape with the client before removing any hair.
markingPoints: Considers the face shape, natural brow and client's wishes
Correct start point: in line with the side of the nose and inner corner of the eye
Correct arch point: through the outer edge of the iris
Correct end point: past the outer corner of the eye; marks and checks both brows match
Agrees the planned shape with the client before starting

essays.stem: Describe how you would shape a client's brows with tweezers, from preparing the area to aftercare.
essays.modelAnswer: I wash my hands and use clean, disinfected or sterilised tweezers. I clean the brow area with a mild antiseptic lotion on cotton and brush the hairs into place. After measuring and agreeing the shape, I stretch the skin gently between two fingers. I grip each hair close to the skin and pull it out quickly in the direction of growth. I remove most hairs from underneath the brow and between the brows, and only stray hairs above it. I work on both brows in turn, brushing them and standing back often to check that they match and that I am not taking off too much. I wipe away loose hairs with damp cotton. At the end I apply a soothing antiseptic lotion and, if needed, a cool compress to calm redness. I advise her to avoid make-up, touching and strong sun on the area for about a day, and I clean and disinfect the tweezers.
markingPoints: Clean, disinfected tweezers and antiseptic on the area before starting
Stretches the skin and removes hairs quickly in the direction of growth
Removes mainly from underneath and between the brows
Checks both brows often so they match and are not over-plucked
Soothing lotion afterwards, correct aftercare advice and tools cleaned

essays.stem: Explain how you would keep a lash and brow treatment hygienic, and why this is so important around the eyes.
essays.modelAnswer: The eyes are delicate and easily infected, and infections such as conjunctivitis spread quickly from person to person. I wash my hands before and after each client and wear gloves if the salon rules or the tint maker ask for them. I use a clean towel and headband for every client. Spoolies, tint brushes, cotton pads, orange sticks and eye shields are used once only and put in a lined, lidded bin. Tweezers, scissors and metal combs are cleaned with soap and water to remove hairs and product, then disinfected for the full time the maker gives, or sterilised. Tint dishes are washed and disinfected. Mixed tint is used once and any left over is thrown away. I take creams out of jars with a clean spatula. I never treat a client with an eye infection. Any blade, such as a brow razor, goes in the sharps box.
markingPoints: Explains why hygiene matters around the eyes (infection spreads easily)
Hand washing, fresh towels and gloves where required
Single-use items used once and disposed of correctly
Metal tools cleaned then disinfected or sterilised; dishes disinfected; leftover tint discarded
Does not treat eye infections; sharps go in the sharps box

essays.stem: Describe the contra-actions that can happen during a lash or brow treatment and the action you would take for each.
essays.modelAnswer: Tint can get into the eye if the client opens her eyes or the shield slips. I would rinse the eye at once with plenty of clean cool water or sterile eye wash, keep rinsing, and advise her to seek medical help if it stays sore or red. An allergic reaction can show as redness, itching, swelling or watering. I would stop, remove the tint gently with cool water, apply a cool compress and advise her to see a doctor. A tint stain on the skin can be removed with a tint stain remover, kept away from the eyes. After tweezing or waxing, the skin may be red or swollen, so I apply a soothing lotion and a cool compress. Small spots of blood can appear; I wear gloves, press with clean cotton and put it in a lined bin. If an adhesive irritates the eye, I remove the lash gently. I record every contra-action on the card.
markingPoints: Tint in the eye: rinse at once with plenty of cool water or eye wash, seek help if needed
Allergic reaction: stop, remove, cool compress, refer to a doctor
Skin staining removed with a stain remover away from the eyes
Redness, swelling or blood spots after tweezing: correct action with gloves
Records every contra-action on the record card

essays.stem: Describe how you would apply and remove a pair of strip lashes.
essays.modelAnswer: I check that the client has no eye infection and no allergy to the adhesive, and she removes her contact lenses if she prefers. I wash my hands. I clean the lashes and lid so they are free of oil. I take the strip lash out of its case with clean tweezers and measure it against her eye. If it is too long, I trim it, usually from the outer end, with clean scissors. I apply a thin line of adhesive along the band and wait a few seconds until it is tacky. With the client looking down, I place the lash as close to her natural lash line as possible, starting in the centre, then pressing the inner and outer corners into place. I check that both eyes match. To remove, I soften the adhesive with a suitable remover on a cotton bud, then peel the strip gently from the outer corner. I never pull it off. Then I clean the lash line.
markingPoints: Checks for infection and adhesive allergy; cleans the lid
Measures and trims the strip to fit the eye
Applies a thin line of adhesive and waits until it is tacky
Places it close to the natural lash line, centre then corners; both eyes match
Removes by softening the adhesive and peeling gently from the outer corner

essays.stem: Explain the aftercare advice you would give after a lash tint, a brow tint and a brow shape, and when the client should come back.
essays.modelAnswer: After a lash tint, the client should avoid rubbing her eyes, remove eye make-up gently with a mild remover, and contact the salon at once if her eyes become red, itchy or sore. After a brow tint, she should avoid harsh scrubs and strong cleansers on the brows, as these can fade the colour. After a brow shape, the skin may be a little red. She should avoid make-up, touching, strong sun, sea bathing and heat on the area for about a day, so that germs do not enter the open follicles. She should not pluck the hairs that grow back, so the shape is not spoilt. A lash tint usually lasts about four to six weeks as the lashes shed and regrow, so she can rebook then, with a new skin test if the maker requires it. Brows usually need tidying every few weeks. I write the advice and the products used on her record card.
markingPoints: Lash tint aftercare: avoid rubbing, gentle make-up removal, report any reaction
Brow tint aftercare: avoid harsh products that fade the colour
Brow shape aftercare: avoid make-up, touching, sun and heat for about a day, and why
Advises when to return (about four to six weeks for tint; brows every few weeks)
Records the advice on the record card

essays.stem: Explain how lash and brow tints and developers should be handled and stored safely in the salon.
essays.modelAnswer: Tints and developers are chemicals, so I follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules every time. I use only products made for lashes and brows, never hair colour for the head, because it can badly injure the eyes. I do not mix different brands. I read the label for the mixing amounts and development time and measure carefully. I mix just before use, in a clean non-metallic dish, and throw away any leftover. I wear gloves if the maker says so, and work in a well-ventilated area. I keep the lids on tightly and wipe up spills at once. Products are stored in a cool, dry, dark place, away from heat and sunlight, in their original labelled containers, and out of reach of children. Hydrogen peroxide is kept away from heat and from things that can burn. I check expiry dates and use the oldest stock first. I know where the eye wash and first aid kit are kept.
markingPoints: Uses only products made for lashes and brows, never head hair colour; no mixing brands
Follows the maker's instructions for mixing and timing; leftover thrown away
Gloves and ventilation as required; spills wiped up
Stored cool, dry and dark, in labelled containers, away from heat
Checks expiry dates and knows where the eye wash and first aid kit are

practical1.title: Lash and brow tint, with a skin test beforehand
practical1.brief: Work in pairs in the Centre's salon and take turns as therapist and client. In a group of five, one member works on a model who has agreed to take part. At least 24 to 48 hours before the practical (or as the maker states), each member carries out a skin test on her client with the same tint and developer, and records it on the record card; the assessor checks the record. Anyone with a positive skin test is not tinted, and her partner works on a model or a practice head instead. On the day, each member holds a consultation, checks for contraindications, chooses a lash and brow colour that suits her client, and tints the lashes and the brows following the maker's instructions. Each member also takes one job for the group: setting up the trolley, timing the tints, taking the photos, or cleaning and disinfecting at the end. Photograph each stage below, as close-ups of the eye or brow area only. Take a whole-face photo only if the client agrees in writing and the Centre allows it. Hand in once for the whole group, with the record cards.
materials: Lash and brow tints in several colours, and the matching developer
Non-metallic tint dishes and disposable tint brushes
Petroleum jelly or barrier cream, and protective eye shields
Eye make-up remover, cotton pads, cotton buds and a bowl of clean water
Couch or reclining chair with towels and headbands
Timer, record cards and eye wash
Gloves, salon disinfectant and a lined, lidded bin
photos: Each member's record card showing the skin test date and result (cover private details)
The trolley set up with the tint, developer and non-metallic dish
Barrier cream and eye shield in place, eyes closed: close-up of one eye
Tint applied to the lashes: close-up
Finished lashes after the tint is removed: close-up
One brow before and after tinting: close-ups
The trolley and tools cleaned and cleared
checklist: Carried out and recorded a skin test at the right time before the tint
Checked for contraindications, and contact lenses were removed
Chose a colour that suits the client's natural hair colour and skin tone
Applied barrier cream to the skin only and placed the eye shield correctly
Mixed the tint as the maker says in a non-metallic dish, and applied it without touching the skin
Timed the development correctly and kept the client's eyes closed
Removed all the tint gently and checked for stains
Gave aftercare advice, threw away leftover tint and cleaned the area
safety: Do not tint anyone with a positive skin test, an eye infection or sore eyes
Use only tints made for lashes and brows, never hair colour for the head
If tint gets into an eye, rinse at once with plenty of clean cool water or eye wash and tell the assessor
Wear gloves as the maker or the Centre's rules say, and keep the room ventilated
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules for mixing and timing

practical2.title: Brow shaping with tweezers, and applying and removing strip lashes
practical2.brief: Work in pairs in the Centre's salon and take turns as therapist and client; in a group of five, one member works on a model who has agreed. Each member holds a consultation, checks for contraindications and agrees a brow shape with her client. She measures both brows with the three-point guide, marks the points, and shapes the brows with tweezers, checking often that they match. She applies a soothing lotion and gives aftercare advice. She then measures, trims and applies a pair of strip lashes, shows them to the assessor, and removes them safely. Each member also takes one job for the group: preparing the tools, checking the adhesive record, taking the photos, or cleaning and disinfecting the tools at the end. Photograph each stage below, as close-ups of the brow or eye area only. Take a whole-face photo only if the client agrees in writing and the Centre allows it. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Clean, disinfected or sterilised slanted tweezers
Orange sticks or brow pencils for measuring, and white pencil for marking
Disposable spoolies, cotton pads and antiseptic and soothing lotions
Strip lashes, lash adhesive (including a latex-free one), and adhesive remover
Small clean scissors and lash applicator or tweezers
